title: Civil Code 1950.5 bad faith retention and nonrefundable deposit ban
requirement: A landlord or the landlord's successor who in bad faith claims or retains a security deposit, or demands replacement security, is liable for statutory damages up to twice the deposit. A lease or rental agreement may not characterize any security as "nonrefundable."
key_value: up to twice the amount of the security
coverage_conditions: This part of the section sets no building or unit limits; it applies to a landlord or the landlord's successors in interest holding a tenant's security deposit under a lease or rental agreement.
penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages; the court may award damages for bad faith; the landlord has the burden of proof as to reasonableness of amounts claimed.
quoted_span: (m) The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
